jobs.description:
Overview
At Mojang Studios, the creators of Minecraft, we are on a mission to build a better world through the power of play.

Why play? Well, play is at the heart of everything we do. It’s the blocky backbone of our games, the core of our development philosophy, and even the origin of our name. From the relentless experimentation of our endlessly inspiring community to the classrooms where Minecraft has become an essential teaching tool, play is the bedrock of our existence.

We enable millions to create and play together, connect people across the globe, and foster a community that is among the most active and passionate in the world. Our community is global and incredibly diverse. When we are developing anything within our franchise, we keep this in mind. We want everyone to not only feel included in Minecraft, but also to see themselves in what we make. Our goal is for the Mojang Studios team to be as diverse as our community.

In the end, it’s the people of Mojang Studios that make this place truly special. When you join, you’ll find yourself in the company of incredibly bright, warm, and creative individuals – all united and working toward a single goal. Come help us reach it!

We are looking for a partner-obsessed Principal Program Manager to lead Partner Developer Relations for the Minecraft Marketplace’s most strategic creator partnerships. In this senior individual-contributor role you own the technical programs, developer-enablement systems, and cross-functional execution that scale how our largest studios build, publish, and grow on the platform.

You set the operating model, standards, and outcomes for partner-facing developer programs, and turn portfolio-wide creator and developer insight into roadmap influence with product and engineering leadership. You are the senior program owner our top studios rely on, driving the tooling, workflows, and feedback loops that anchor the majority of Marketplace ecosystem health. You blend deep program ownership with real technical fluency, and you are measured on the delivery, adoption, and health of the partner developer programs you own.

- Own the strategy and delivery of the top-tier partner developer program portfolio: define scope, roadmap, milestones, and success metrics for the technical programs serving our largest, most strategic, franchise-defining creator partners.
- Define the developer-relations operating model and quality bar: set program standards, onboarding and enablement workflows, tooling requirements, and the KPIs and guardrails that keep quality, safety, and player trust non-negotiable.
- Serve as the senior voice of the creator and developer: synthesize portfolio-wide feedback into a prioritized, structured signal that shapes the Creator Success roadmap directly with product and engineering leadership.
- Act as the senior program advisor to top studios, driving cross-team resolution of the high-stakes blockers that put strategic launches at risk, and owning the programs behind special projects, featured placement, and platform enablement within defined thresholds.
- Own executive-level program reviews and escalations: run business/program reviews with our leadership and partner founders and executives, and act as accountable escalation owner during safety, payout, outage, or PR-sensitive events.
- Drive competitive and retention strategy at the program level, defending against competing platforms (Roblox, Fortnite/UEFN, Unity, Fab) through better developer experience, tooling, and enablement at portfolio scale.

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day and we need you as a Regional Critical Environment (CE) Program Manager.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I CE Program Manager, you will perform a key role in delivering and managing the critical environment infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

jobs.title: Business Program Manager
jobs.description:
Overview
Microsoft is on a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Our culture is centred on embracing a growth mindset, a theme of inspiring excellence, and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best each day. In doing so, we create life-changing innovations that impact billions of lives around the world. You can help us achieve our mission.
Do you want to work in a company that is transforming the world? How about working on cutting-edge issues, with world class clients and the support of a global community of professionals? If you are ready to work directly with business leaders and their teams to solve problems and drive change, then a career with the Microsoft National Security Team is for you.

The UK National Security Team (NST) is a small, high-impact group of security experts working at the intersection of compliance, technology, policy and business strategy. NST partners closely with sales, engineering, legal and business leaders to enable Microsoft’s most strategic customer opportunities while managing regulatory and reputational risk.
We have an immediate opening for a highly motivated and experienced Information Security Manager to join the NST, which sits within the UK & Ireland Legal Affairs team and National Security Team, and supports compliance with government personnel, project, information and facility-security requirements.  The position is based at our offices in Reading and will report to a Principal Corporate Counsel in Legal Affairs.
Role Purpose:

The Information Security Manager is responsible for information security governance, assurance and operational security support across Microsoft UK Public Safety and National Security activities. The role helps ensure compliance with UK Government security policy, contractual obligations and customer security requirements.
The post holder acts as a trusted information security adviser to programme teams, engineering, sales, legal, security stakeholders and leadership. They translate complex regulatory and contractual security requirements into practical controls that enable secure, compliant delivery throughout the programme lifecycle.
A key priority is identifying security requirements early and reducing avoidable delivery friction without weakening compliance. This work supports customer confidence, programme delivery and revenue realisation by reducing the risk of contractual breaches, accreditation delays, security incidents and unplanned remediation.

Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities - Information Security Governance & Policy

- Define, maintain and implement information and operational security policies, standards and procedures aligned with UK Government policy, Microsoft requirements and contractual obligations.
- Act as a subject matter expert on information security governance for UK national security programmes.
- Translate government and customer security requirements into scalable, operationally workable controls.
- Provide independent advice and constructive challenge where security, contractual or compliance obligations may be at risk.
- Support audits, inspections, assurance reviews and customer accreditation activity.
- Maintain awareness of evolving UK Government security policy, regulation and the national security threat landscape.

Programme Security Governance & Assurance
- Provide information security leadership across the programme lifecycle, from early engagement and tenders through delivery and operation.
- Work with programme management and engineering teams to embed security in programme design and delivery.
- Review and interpret Security Aspects Letters, Security Grading Guides, contractual security schedules and security flow-down requirements.
- Support the development and maintenance of Security Management Plans, procedures and assurance documentation.
- Help establish or participate in customer and programme Security Working Groups.
- Ensure information security risks are identified, documented, reviewed and escalated through appropriate governance.

Contract Security:
- Engage with sales, account and bid teams to identify security requirements early.
- Review relevant DEFCON, Defence Standard and customer-specific security requirements.
- Advise on security obligations within Statements of Work and related contractual documents.
- Identify delivery and compliance risks associated with proposed commitments or solutions.
- Support customer discussions where security requirements require clarification or negotiation.
- Ensure agreed security requirements transition effectively into programme delivery.

Information Security Risk Management:
- Support security risk assessments across UK national security programmes.
- Review programme risk registers and evaluate the effectiveness of proposed mitigations.
- Ensure significant security risks are escalated to the appropriate risk owner or governance body.
- Provide information security assurance to programme leadership and senior stakeholders.
- Support remediation, assurance assessments, accreditation reviews and security testing.
- Monitor recurring issues and identify opportunities to improve controls, processes and programme security maturity.
- Promote consistent, evidence-based security risk management across programmes.

Information Protection & Secure Collaboration:
- Provide guidance on the handling, storage, sharing, transfer, retention and disposal of sensitive information.
- Advise on the suitability of Microsoft tooling and collaboration environments for sensitive programme activity.
- Support secure document management and customer-specific information handling requirements.
- Advise on restricted collaboration environments, ethical firewalls and information-separation controls.
- Help ensure sensitive information is handled in line with contractual and government requirements and need-to-know principles

Security Incident Management:
- Provide information security advice and support during security incidents affecting relevant programmes.
- Ensure potential incidents are identified, recorded and escalated appropriately.
- Support proportionate, independent incident investigations where required.
- Assess security, customer and contractual implications.
- Recommend containment, remediation and risk-reduction actions.
- Produce or support incident reports and after-action reviews.
- Ensure lessons learned are reflected in programme controls, guidance and training.

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement:
- Act as an information security point of contact for UK national security programmes.
- Build trusted relationships with programme teams, Engineering, Sales, Legal and Microsoft security stakeholders.
- Engage with UK Government, defence and national security customers on security assurance and compliance matters.
- Represent Microsoft at Security Working Groups, assurance meetings and security governance forums.
- Develop security briefings for programme leadership, senior executives and customers.
- Communicate complex security risks and requirements clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
- Promote security as a practical business enabler.

Other areas:
- Develop positive relationships with legal colleagues within the UK & Ireland Legal Affairs team, with UK government affairs colleagues and with colleagues in the wider EMEA region to coach and advise on compliance issues.
- Engage with legal and business colleagues to identify and share best practices.
- Support programme-specific security briefings, training and awareness material.
- Support and collaborate with NST Personnel Security Controller and Facility Manager.
- Develop positive relationships with customers, and partners to protect and advocate for Microsoft’s interests.
- Collaborate with service providers to develop strategies and innovative solutions to address business issues and achieve business objectives.
- Some knowledge of Defence exports compliance issues would be an advantage but not essential. The role includes support to project teams and liaison with Microsoft’s international trade specialists on matters involving US and other applicable export-control regimes.
- Identify gaps and inefficiencies in security processes and lead proportionate improvements
- Use AI solutions to scale work and drive continuous improvement.
- Monitor emerging risks, policy developments and operational security trends.

Attendance at our Reading offices as required.
International travel will be required from time to time.

Qualifications
Required qualifications:

- Demonstrable experience in information security, operational security, programme security or a government security role.
- The successful candidate is a sole UK National and hold, or be able to obtain and maintain, the UK Government security clearance required for the role (DV).
- Knowledge of UK Government security policy, security controls and government information handling requirements.
- Demonstrable experience supporting large, complex programmes for UK Government, defence or national security customers.

Preferred qualifications:

- Experience interpreting contractual security requirements and translating them into practical operational controls.
- Experience managing information security risk, assurance or accreditation activities.
- Stakeholder-management skills, including engagement with leaders, customers and multidisciplinary delivery teams and ability to  establish a “trusted advisor” relationship.
- An ability to work independently while also being a collaborator with the ability to work with colleagues based in different locations.
- A high tolerance for ambiguity and change.
- Passion for technology, the potential of digital transformation and Microsoft’s diverse range of products and services
- Desirable CISSP, CISM, CCSP.

jobs.title: EHS Electrical & Process Safety Program Manager
jobs.location: United States, Multiple Locations, Multiple Locations; United States, Georgia, Atlanta; United States, Texas, San Antonio
jobs.description:
Overview
Microsoft Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) is seeking an EHS Electrical & Process Safety Program Manager to help prevent EHS incidents through disciplined hazard identification, risk assessment, and application of process safety principles across datacenter facilities, infrastructure, and emerging technologies. This role sits within Global EHS Engineering, Strategy & Standards (ESS) organization and partners closely with EHS program owners, regional EHS teams, and Datacenter Engineering and Operations to enable a safe and healthy working environment across Microsoft’s global datacenter portfolio. The successful candidate will identify hazards, analyze consequences and risks, and recommend practical, engineering‑based controls to mitigate risk in alignment with Microsoft standards and regulatory requirements, supporting the safe delivery of Microsoft infrastructure technologies worldwide. This is an individual contributor (IC4) role requiring strong technical judgment, cross‑functional collaboration, and program execution skills.
This role is available to candidates anywhere within the US. Successful candidates who live within 50 miles of a Microsoft hub will be required to work from the office a minimum of 3 days per week.  Hub locations - Redmond, WA, Atlanta, GA, San Antonio, TX, Phoenix, AZ, or Washington DC.

Responsibilities
- Provide electrical safety expertise supporting the design and deployment of new hardware, facilities, systems, equipment, and machinery.
- Own or co-own electrical safety program elements (standards, training expectations, inspection/assessment criteria) consistent with Microsoft electrical safety requirements.
- Leads ambiguous, cross-region electrical safety problems to resolution; sets technical direction for program content and standards.
- Influences design/operations stakeholders through data, risk framing, and practical engineering controls.
- Review electrical design artifacts relevant to safety: one-lines, protection/coordination intent, equipment room access/clearance impacts, and maintainability constraints
- Perform Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) process safety risk assessments for existing facilities, new facility designs, and emerging technologies.
- Apply process safety and hazard analysis methodologies (e.g. HAZID, HAZOP, etc.) to identify hazards, evaluate risk, and recommend effective controls.
- Develop, implement, and continuously improve global EHS programs to reduce process and operational safety risk.
- Partner with datacenter engineering teams to integrate technical safety considerations into designs and enable safe operation of facilities and infrastructure.
- Analyze EHS performance metrics and indicators to identify trends, prioritize risk‑reduction opportunities, and inform program improvements.
- Conduct inspections, assessments, and design reviews to verify compliance with applicable regulations, standards, and Microsoft policies.
- Perform workplace risk and exposure assessments across electrical, mechanical, and operational hazard categories.
- Support incident investigations, including root cause analysis and identification, communication, and implementation of corrective and preventive actions.
- Embody our culture and values .

Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or Mechatronics  with significant, demonstrated electrical engineering experience, including work with power systems, electrical design, or electrical safety in complex environments, related field AND 4+ years experience in environmental health and safety worldwide Regulations OR equivalent experience.
Background Check Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
- Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Additional or preferred qualifications
- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or Mechatronics with significant, demonstrated electrical engineering experience, including work with power systems, electrical design, or electrical safety in complex environments.
- 5+ years of experience in electrical engineering, electrical safety, or power systems engineering in datacenter, industrial, or other complex infrastructure environments, including demonstrated experience reviewing electrical systems, conducting electrical hazard risk assessments, and recommending engineering and operational controls.
- Demonstrated expertise in electrical safety, including hazard identification, risk assessment, and control design for electrical systems, equipment, and high‑energy infrastructure. This includes medium-voltage / high-energy distribution, switchgear, UPS, battery rooms/energy storage, generators, commissioning/maintenance interface,
- Demonstrated experience applying applicable electrical safety regulations and standards—including NFPA 70, NFPA 70E, OSHA electrical safety requirements (including 29 CFR 1910 Subpart S), and IEEE 1584—to electrical design reviews, hazard assessments, and operational risk reduction.
- Working knowledge of process hazard analysis (PHA) and risk assessment methodologies (e.g., HAZID, HAZOP, What‑If, FMEA, or equivalent) applied to engineering and operational risk.
- Experience translating technical electrical and process safety risks into practical, implementable recommendations for engineering and operational stakeholders.
- Strong analytical, problem‑solving, organizational, and technical communication skills, with the ability to influence safety outcomes through collaboration rather than authority.
- Experience supporting safety in complex, high‑energy infrastructure environments, such as datacenters, industrial facilities, or mission‑critical systems.
- PE (Electrical) or equivalent registration
- Professional certification or registration in electrical safety, safety engineering, or an EHS‑related discipline.
- 5+ years of experience performing process safety and/or EHS risk assessments, including application of Process Safety Management (PSM) principles and risk management tools.
- Additional degree in Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, or a related field.
- Experience influencing design and safety outcomes through cross‑functional collaboration in global organizations.

Internship Opportunity: Business Operations & Management Assistant Coordinator
Start Date: November 2026

Microsoft's European Government Affairs (EGA) organization is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Business, Operations and Management Assistant Coordinator to join its Brussels-based team. This is an ideal opportunity for an early-career candidate who is eager to develop practical experience in business operations, financial coordination, procurement and executive support within an international and fast-paced environment.

The purpose of Microsoft's European Government Affairs organization is to build relationships and strengthen dialogue with European stakeholders in support of the European digital and broader policy agenda.

Finance and Operations

jobs.title: Customer Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Overview
Organization Summary:
If you love the pursuit of excellence and are inspired by the challenges that come through driving innovations that impact how the world lives, works, and plays, then we invite you to learn more about Microsoft Operations - and the value we deliver across Microsoft, our partners, and our customers. We offer unique opportunities to work on interesting global projects in an environment that appreciates diversity, focuses on talent development, and recognizes and rewards great work. We make doing business with Microsoft easy.
Microsoft Enterprise Direct Services, within Microsoft Business Operations, provides direct and centralized operations services for Direct Enterprise Agreement customers to transact with Microsoft. We are accountable to design and executing transactional services across the Enterprise customer lifecycle. We relentlessly pursue process efficiency, timeliness, quality, and compliance, all while providing world class Customer experience. We are looking for team members to join our team to focused on delivering an exceptional Customer experience with deep expertise in Contracting, Order Management, Billing and Supplier Management and Customer relationship experience.
Position Description:
The Customer Operations Manager is responsible for customer-facing licensing solutions and must be a subject matter expert within our Volume Licensing concepts and processes. The Customer Operations Manager will provide direct, front line transactional support for Microsoft Field sellers and our customers. The Customer Operations Manager is responsible for ensuring adherence with the Microsoft account plan, ensuring deliverables are executed on time and of high quality for our customers.
The Customer Operations Manager role requires fluency in both English and Japanese to effectively support our Japan-based clients and ensure smooth communication across all transactional and customer service activities. You will be expected to interact directly with Japanese-speaking customers and internal stakeholders.
The role will also provide fantastic opportunities to lead and shape next generation experiences for internal stakeholders and end customers. Are you ready to make an impact in this exciting and challenging role?

Responsibilities
Contracting and Order Management  ​
- Deal and Contract Validation:  Manage the validation and execution of agreements and post sales lifecycle transactions enabling accuracy in downstream financial processes followed by compliant issuance of customer contracts in accordance with Policies, Global and SOX approved deal financials.
- Pipeline Management:  Manage critical deal lists on a monthly and quarterly basis ​ in alignment with expectations with the Sales, Sales Excellence and key Subsidiary sales stakeholders on all critical deals for the month ​​ .

Billing Management ​
- Billing Execution:  ensuring accurate and compliant order and invoice approval and dispatch (standard and local) to maximize cash flow and collectability for all invoices. ​
- Credit Approval management:  including orchestration of all Finance exception approvals on high value credits and execution of all credits and associated rebills. ​
- Billing status and risk management:  including tracking and communicating contract billing status to key stakeholders highlighting risks with contractual requirements, customer PO coverage, customer sign offs and credit/payment status.  ​

Customer Service
- Serve as the primary point of contact for all operational customer service inquiries, concerns, and issues.
- Oversee the daily operations of the customer service team to ensure quality standards are met and maintained.
- Monitor customer service metrics and KPIs to identify areas of improvement and implement strategies to boost performance.
- Handle escalated customer service issues and complaints in a professional and efficient manner.
- Work closely with other departments to resolve customer issues and ensure a positive customer experience.
- Develop and implement processes and procedures to streamline the customer service operation.
- Stay up-to-date on industry trends and best practices to ensure the customer service team is providing the highest level of service possible.
- Generate reports on customer service metrics and activity for senior leader consumption and monthly business reviews.

Operations Excellence: Optimization and Process improvement ​
- Acts as a thought leader to drive consistency in processes, capabilities, and services meeting performance expectations for consistency, accuracy, simplification, and timeliness of delivery ​ .
- Trusted advisor for customers and internal clients on operational processes and capabilities, and provides efficient, scalable operational solutions across a portfolio of accounts ​ .

Stakeholder Management (Field, Partners, Customers)  ​
- Uses voice of customer frameworks and metrics to identify trends and influences across multiple customers and internal groups.

Qualifications
Required Experience/Minimum Qualifications
- Fluency in Japanese, with the ability to communicate effectively with both external and internal customers/stakeholders, including writing, reading, and speaking.
- Japanese language certifications, such as JLPT (N2 or higher), BJT, or J.TEST, are preferred to validate language proficiency in a business context.
- 6+ years of work experience in contracting & order management, pipeline management, & billing execution, with a focus on financial accuracy, compliance, and risk management.
- Expertise in contract validation, pipeline management, credit approval, and billing management, with strong capabilities in customer service, stakeholder engagement, process optimization, and operations excellence.
- Leverages AI to drive operational excellence, accelerate customer outcomes, and enable data-driven decision making.

- Demonstrates practical application of AI tools to improve productivity, customer engagement, and business impact.

- Proficiency in data-driven decision-making, using KPIs to monitor performance, and acting as a trusted advisor to internal and external customers.
- Bachelor’s degree in business, Operations, Finance or related field AND operations, program management or process management work experience
- OR equivalent experience.

- On site presence minimum 3 days/week.

Preferred Qualifications
- 4+ years of experience in customer service operations, managing escalations, improving service metrics, & implementing process improvements to streamline operations.
- Experience with similar industry Business Value deal constructions.
- Experience with Microsoft licensing concepts, including contracts, quotes and invoices, as well as evaluation and review of complex proposals, agreements, and amendments.
- Experience providing direct support for Microsoft Volume Licensing sales and support lifecycle

This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. If you need assistance with religious accommodations and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application process, read more about requesting accommodations.

The role will also provide fantastic opportunities to lead and shape next generation experiences for internal stakeholders and end customers. Are you ready to make an impact in this exciting and challenging role?

- Billing status and risk management:  including tracking and communicating contract billing status to key stakeholders highlighting risks with contractual requirements, customer PO coverage, customer sign offs and credit/payment status.  ​

jobs.title: Datacenter Security Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Overview
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day and we need you as a Datacenter Security Operations Manager.

As a Datacenter Security Operations Manager in CO+I Physical Security, you will be part of a global team dedicated to delivering the most trustworthy security program to protect the personnel, infrastructure, data, and confidential information foundational to the Microsoft Cloud. You will be accountable for physical security operations at datacenters and other related facilities within your applicable region and will collaborate with the vendor security guarding staff to meet collective security requirements and provide security capabilities, anticipate site specific insecurity and security disruption (e.g., life safety, business operations, reputation) and lead discussions on developing strategies for mitigating risks and responding to residual risks. You will communicate risk analysis findings and root cause analysis reports to internal and external stakeholders and leaders. This opportunity will allow you to accelerate your career growth, develop deeper physical security acumen and global security program management. The Datacenter Security Operations Manager must be located in the applicable region and will work from an agreed upon datacenter location.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a Datacenter Security Operations Manager you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development for all employees and offers trainings and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion trainings and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Do you want to empower billions across the world? Come and join us in CO+I and be at the forefront of the action!

Responsibilities
Security Program Management
- Oversee the implementation of physical security policies and procedures at applicable datacenters, ensuring Microsoft’s physical security vendor guard force has the resources and information to deliver physical security services that meet Microsoft and customer requirements to protect people, information, and critical infrastructure.
- With minimal assistance, performs analysis to detect security threats, alerts, or risks and escalates to critical incident response team and/or external authorities, if necessary. With minimal assistance, implements security protocols to support the physical protection of company personnel and assets. With minimal assistance, delivers and maintains security programs in areas of responsibility.
- Partner with datacenter operations, security systems and other Microsoft stakeholders to ensure secure and continuous operations while maintaining a One Team, One Microsoft environment.
- Continuously improve the efficiency and maturity of the overall physical security program at Microsoft datacenters, seeking data and recommending strategies and ideas to reduce churn, optimizing resources including budget management and forecasting, implement creative solutions to problems, scale, automate and simplify process whenever possible.

Security Leadership
- Receive escalations/notifications of physical security and business impacting events and appropriately triage, ensure that regional leadership is kept informed through regular communication as appropriate and that the necessary personnel for managing an incident respond effectively.
- On-call 24x7x365 and will travel periodically as planned or unplanned within or outside of assigned city/metropolitan area.
- With minimal supervision, contributes to collaborative efforts with stakeholders to support security capabilities. Supports risk identification for datacenter insecurity and security disruption (e.g., life safety, business operations, reputation) to assist decision-makers in mitigating risks and responding to residual risks. With minimal supervision, summarizes and reports risk analysis to internal stakeholders and leaders.

Other
- Embody our culture and values .

Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
- 4+ years' experience in Security Program or Program Management or related field

While not required, we look for the following Preferred Qualifications:
- Bachelor's Degree in Business Risks or related field AND 8+ years' experience in Security Program or Program Management - OR equivalent experience.

- Industry security certifications such as CPP, PSP, or other relevant security certification

Background Check Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
- Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

jobs.title: Datacenter Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Overview
As a Datacenter Operations Manager , you will lead the day-to-day operations of a critical datacenter environment, ensuring the highest standards of reliability, availability, safety, and operational excellence. You will oversee teams responsible for infrastructure operations, maintenance, and service delivery while driving continuous improvement across processes, capacity management, and operational readiness. This role offers the opportunity to have a direct impact on the performance and scalability of the technology infrastructure that powers global services, working in a fast-paced environment where innovation, collaboration, and customer focus are essential to success.

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Datacenter Operations Manager (DCOM), you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development for all employees and offers trainings and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion trainings and events, and professional certifications.

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 100 datacenters and 1 million servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Do you want to empower billions across the world? Come and join us in CO+I and be at the forefront of the action!

Responsibilities

- Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team, creating an environment of accountability, empowerment, continuous learning, and professional growth.
- Attract, retain, and develop talent by aligning team capabilities, career aspirations, and business needs to build a sustainable workforce.
- Establish clear objectives, priorities, and performance expectations, driving execution and adaptation to changing business requirements.
- Oversee the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of critical data center infrastructure, ensuring adherence to operational, safety, and regulatory standards.
- Provide technical leadership across Critical Environment (CE) infrastructure, including high-voltage and low-voltage electrical systems, UPS and battery systems, standby generators, fuel systems, electrical distribution, cooling infrastructure, BMS, EPMS, and fire detection and suppression systems.
- Ensure compliance with service level agreements, operational processes, maintenance standards, and all applicable regulatory and safety requirements.
- Lead and govern maintenance activities, including the execution and review of MOPs, SOPs, EOPs, permits to work, change management activities, and operational risk assessments.
- Manage vendor, landlord, contractor, and stakeholder relationships to ensure operational excellence, service reliability, and effective service delivery.
- Drive service quality, infrastructure availability, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement initiatives across data center operations.
- Lead major incident management activities, coordinating response efforts, recovery actions, root cause investigations, and corrective and preventive measures.
- Identify, assess, and mitigate operational, electrical, mechanical, and facility-related risks that could impact safety, service availability, or business continuity.
- Support operational readiness, capacity planning, commissioning activities, lifecycle management, and long-term infrastructure strategy for critical facility assets.
- Plan and manage budgets, forecasting, resource allocation, and operational priorities while maintaining fiscal responsibility and efficiency.
- Partner cross-functionally to deliver strategic initiatives, support environmental health and safety programs, strengthen risk management practices, and achieve business objectives.
- Foster a culture of safety, quality, accountability, collaboration, and customer obsession throughout all operational activities.
- Remove operational barriers, proactively resolve issues, and implement improvements to enhance reliability, performance, and business continuity.
- Serve as a trusted advisor to stakeholders by communicating risks, dependencies, operational impacts, costs, and mitigation strategies to enable informed decision-making.
- Ensure teams are prepared to respond to and recover from incidents affecting mission-critical infrastructure, maintaining operational resilience and service continuity.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
- Bachelor's Degree or equivalent AND experience of mission-critical service management (e.g., providing IT services, manufacturing, warehouse, retail, military, or managing physical operations in an IT).
- Experience in critical environment infrastructures ( e.g., mechanical systems, electrical systems, controls systems)
- Proven experience leading, directly managing, and influencing a diverse organization across multiple disciplines and platforms.
- This role requires fluency in reading, writing, and conversational French and English, as all business operations and stakeholder communications are conducted in these languages

Background Check Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
- Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Enterprise-level experience managing large scale and complex projects/programs AND experience in physical IT infrastructures (e.g., Servers, SANs, Networking, Capacity, DC Rack/Enclosures, structured cabling) AND Experience managing budget $500k+.
- Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Math, Telecommunications, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or related field.
- Experience of managing managers, leading diverse, technical workforce or managing global and virtual teams.
- Applicable certifications: ASICS/Inventory Control, CompTIA, Microsoft, Network Certifications, CCNA Certifications, ITIL v3 Foundation, Microsoft Operations Framework (MOF) Certifications, Leadership Development Certifications, PMP, CDCP.

jobs.title: Datacenter Security Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Overview
Overview
Microsoft's Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) organisation powers the infrastructure supporting Microsoft's cloud services. Datacenter Physical Security is responsible for protecting people, facilities, assets and critical infrastructure.
The Datacenter Security Operations Manager (DSOM) leads day-to-day physical security operations across assigned Microsoft datacenters, campuses and metro locations. The role provides operational leadership, security subject-matter expertise and oversight of contracted security services, ensuring physical security measures remain effective, resilient and aligned with Microsoft policies, standards and operational requirements.
The ideal candidate will work closely with Datacenter Operations, Engineering, Environmental Health and Safety, Compliance, Investigations, Security Design and Delivery, lease providers, construction partners and contracted security service providers.

Responsibilities
Security Operations Leadership
- Lead and oversee physical security operations across assigned datacenters, campuses and metro locations.
- Ensure security programmes, procedures, post orders and site-specific instructions are implemented consistently.
- Assess the effectiveness of access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, alarms, physical barriers, screening checkpoints and other security measures.
- Conduct regular site visits, security reviews and operational assessments to verify compliance with established security baselines.
- Monitor operational performance, identify gaps and drive corrective and preventive actions.
- Maintain accurate security documentation, operational records and leadership reporting.

Incident Management and Investigations
- Lead on-site response to security incidents, threats and significant operational events.
- Coordinate response activities with Datacenter Operations, security service providers, lease providers, internal security teams and local authorities, as appropriate.
- Support security investigations, fact-finding, evidence preservation, root-cause analysis and after-action reviews.
- Ensure incident and investigation records are prepared accurately and actions are tracked to closure.
- Apply lessons learned from incidents to strengthen operational controls and procedures.
- Support security bridge calls and provide timely situation updates to security leadership and stakeholders.

Risk, Compliance and Audit Readiness
- Conduct or support physical security risk assessments and develop practical mitigation plans.
- Maintain audit readiness across assigned locations.
- Coordinate audit evidence and support internal, external, customer and regulatory audit activities.
- Present site physical security posture during audits and operational reviews.
- Track audit observations, risk actions and remediation commitments to closure.
- Monitor changes in the local threat and operating environment and recommend appropriate adjustments to security posture.

Vendor Governance and Performance
- Provide operational oversight of contracted security service providers and ensure services are delivered in line with contractual and programme expectations.
- Establish a structured governance cadence with vendor security management, including operational reviews, performance discussions and action tracking.
- Review security incidents, staffing readiness, training, procedure compliance, technology issues and service-delivery risks.
- Hold service providers accountable for timely remediation of operational gaps while maintaining professional working relationships.
- Support security staffing readiness for new sites, checkpoints, operational expansions and changes in site requirements.

Datacenter Delivery and Change Management
- Support physical security readiness for new datacenters, site expansions, beneficial-use activities, early access, checkpoint deployments and security lockdowns.
- Participate in security integration, end-to-end readiness and transition discussions.
- Review security readiness requirements, implementation plans, site start-up activities and unresolved security issues.
- Coordinate with Security Design and Delivery, project teams, Datacenter Operations and security service providers to transition new facilities into steady-state operations.
- Participate in security-related projects, technology deployments and changes to physical security infrastructure or procedures.

Stakeholder Management
- Build effective relationships with Datacenter Operations, Engineering, Environmental Health and Safety, Compliance, Security Design and Delivery, Investigations, lease providers and other internal stakeholders.
- Provide physical security expertise and risk-based guidance to business partners.
- Communicate security risks, operational constraints and mitigations clearly to management and stakeholders.
- Influence cross-functional teams to achieve security outcomes without direct organisational authority.
- Represent physical security in operational governance, readiness and business-review forums.

Crisis Management and Operational Resilience
- Participate actively in the local crisis management structure.
- Support emergency preparedness, crisis-response exercises and business-continuity activities.
- Provide on-site security leadership during significant incidents or periods of elevated risk.
- Ensure contracted security teams understand and execute their responsibilities under emergency and crisis-management plans.
- Identify resilience gaps and support practical contingency and recovery measures.

Security Culture and Continuous Improvement
- Promote security awareness, vigilance and responsible reporting across the datacenter community.
- Support initiatives addressing insider risk, access control, protection of data-bearing devices and other physical security risks.
- Analyse incidents, trends, security metrics and operational feedback to identify improvement opportunities.
- Contribute to regional security programmes, standardisation and the adoption of effective security practices.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications
- 14+ years of professional experience in physical security, security operations, critical-infrastructure protection, military service, law enforcement, investigations, intelligence, risk management or a closely related field.
- A minimum of 3 years of corporate security experience within a private-sector organisation operating established security governance, compliance, reporting and stakeholder-management processes.
- Demonstrated experience managing physical security operations in a complex, high-availability or critical-infrastructure environment.
- Experience overseeing contracted security services, guarding operations or third-party service providers.
- Experience managing security incidents, investigations, operational risks and corrective actions.
- Working knowledge of physical security systems, including access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, alarms and screening technologies.
- Experience supporting security audits, compliance reviews, risk assessments and remediation programmes.
- Strong stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to work across operations, engineering, compliance, facilities, project and vendor teams.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of incident reports, risk summaries and leadership updates.
- Ability to make sound, risk-based decisions in time-sensitive and operationally demanding situations.
- Ability to travel between supported datacentre locations as business needs require and provide on-site support during significant incidents or critical operational activities.

Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in security management, risk management, business administration, engineering, criminal justice, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
- Experience supporting datacenters, cloud infrastructure, telecommunications, utilities, manufacturing, energy or another critical-infrastructure sector.
- Experience working within a multinational corporation or similarly complex organisation.
- Experience in new-site delivery, security commissioning, operational readiness, checkpoint deployment or site lockdown activities.
- Experience in crisis management, emergency response, business continuity or operational resilience.
- Experience managing multi-site security operations or security programmes across a metro or regional footprint.
- Professional certification such as Certified Protection Professional (CPP), Physical Security Professional (PSP), Professional Certified Investigator (PCI), Project Management Professional (PMP), or an equivalent recognised credential.
- Working knowledge of relevant Indian regulatory, statutory and operational requirements applicable to private security and critical infrastructure.
- We encourage candidates to apply even if they do not meet every qualification listed. If your experience is closely aligned with this role and you are passionate about protecting critical infrastructure, we welcome your application.

Overview
MCAPS-Core accelerates customer outcomes and business growth. By uniting product, engineering, marketing, sales, customer success, and partners around a common customer mission, we help customers realize value faster and turn innovation into measurable business impact. Through deep technical expertise and differentiated go-to-market execution, we win competitively, capture market share, and scale repeatable growth motions. We differentiate through value creation - delivering world-class, AI-powered customer experiences that accelerate adoption, strengthen loyalty, and create sustainable competitive advantage, driving growth that outpaces the market.

As the Business Program Manager – Capacity Automation & Backend Tools , you will help improve and scale the processes, data flows, integrations, and tools that support how Microsoft prioritizes and allocates AI and non-AI Azure capacity as one unified business. You will translate operational needs into clear requirements and partner with Engineering to deliver practical, reliable automation.

This is a hands-on program role at the technical core of Capacity Shared Services. You will manage defined workstreams, coordinate dependencies, validate solutions with users, and use data to improve quality, cycle time, and adoption across intake, prioritization, decisioning, reporting, and governance workflows.

The role sits within Capacity Shared Services in MCAPS Core, where AI and non-AI capacity are managed under the One Capacity approach. You will collaborate with Engineering, Finance, data, and operations partners to maintain a prioritized tooling backlog, implement reusable solutions, and apply Microsoft Copilot and purpose-built agents to reduce manual effort.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities
Business Program Management
- Lead end-to-end capacity automation and operational tooling programs, ensuring successful execution against business goals, timelines, and deliverables.
- Manage complex workstreams across multiple stakeholders, balancing priorities, dependencies, risks, and business outcomes.
- Drive operational rigor through structured program management practices, governance, and stakeholder alignment.

Process Improvement
- Identify opportunities to streamline and automate business processes, reduce manual effort, and improve operational efficiency.
- Implement scalable solutions that enhance reliability, consistency, and effectiveness of the Capacity Operating System.
- Leverage data and stakeholder feedback to continuously improve workflows and operating models.

Requirements Analysis
- Translate business needs into clear requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and functional specifications.
- Partner with stakeholders to prioritize initiatives and ensure solutions align with strategic business objectives.
- Drive requirements gathering and validation activities throughout the solution lifecycle.

Project Management

Data Analytics
- Use data, reporting, and operational metrics to inform prioritization, decision-making, and process optimization.
- Analyze trends and performance indicators to identify opportunities for efficiency and business impact.
- Develop insights that improve operational effectiveness and support strategic planning.

Business Insight
- Apply deep understanding of capacity allocation, governance, and operational processes to improve business performance.
- Identify opportunities to enhance organizational effectiveness through process, tooling, and operational improvements.
- Recommend solutions that balance business needs, operational requirements, and long-term scalability.

Stakeholder Management and Influence
- Build trusted partnerships across technical and business organizations.
- Influence decisions and drive alignment without direct authority.
- Communicate complex concepts clearly and effectively to diverse audiences.

Change Management
- Drive adoption of new processes, tools, automation capabilities, and governance standards.
- Develop documentation, communications, and enablement materials to support organizational change.
- Champion continuous improvement and operational transformation initiatives.

Operational Excellence
- Establish and maintain data quality, governance, reliability, and process standards.
- Create scalable documentation, best practices, and operational frameworks.
- Support sustainable operations through continuous monitoring and optimization.

Artificial Intelligence & Copilot Adoption
- Leverage Microsoft Copilot and AI-powered solutions to improve productivity, analysis, documentation, and operational execution.
- Identify opportunities to apply AI technologies to automate recurring workflows and enhance business outcomes.
- Promote innovative approaches that increase operational scale and efficiency.

Preferred:
- Experience with datacenter, compute, or infrastructure capacity management systems and tooling used to plan, allocate, monitor, and scale capacity.

- Experience in cloud computing, including experience working for or with major cloud providers, cloud customers, partners, or the broader cloud infrastructure industry.

- Familiarity with AI capacity planning, AI infrastructure, GPU compute, large-scale model requirements, Generative AI, Agentic AI, and the supply constraints that influence AI workload prioritization and customer outcomes.

jobs.description:
Overview
Team Overview

The Source-to-Pay (S2P) Solutions Team within Global Payout Solutions, Finance Operations, delivers technology capabilities that enable AI transformation across Source-to-Pay and Travel and Expense experiences. The team bridges business vision and engineering to create scalable, automated solutions that improve purchasing, supplier management, contracts, risk, compliance, and employee experiences.

Role Summary

The Sr. Procurement Operations Manager for Supplier Management serves as a Program Manager and Subject Matter Expert for the Procurement Supplier Performance Scorecard, the enterprise tool and process used to monitor managed supplier spend across books of business. The role partners with the Supplier Enablement team to enable program strategy, and leads planning, execution, automation, and roadmap development in partnership with internal engineering partners.

This role applies critical judgment, business analysis, and data-driven decision-making to identify opportunities, solve complex problems, and improve supplier performance programs. The successful candidate will connect business priorities, operational processes, data, and technology; define measurable outcomes; and influence cross-functional stakeholders to adopt changes that increase preferred-supplier utilization, strengthen supplier accountability, and accelerate corrective action for performance, compliance, and risk concerns.

Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities

Program Strategy, Planning, and Design

- Lead the Procurement Supplier Performance Scorecard as the accountable program manager and subject matter expert, enabling program vision, strategy, scope, governance, requirements, and the plan of record.

- Use user feedback, business insights, industry trends, and current- and future-state analysis to identify new capabilities and improvements, map end-to-end systems and process dependencies, and assess impacts across supplier performance, Source-to-Pay workflows, data, contracts, risk, compliance, and related platforms.

- Define success criteria and performance measures—including objectives and key results, key performance indicators, service levels, adoption, usage, quality, impact, and effectiveness—and embed security, privacy, compliance, and control requirements from initiation through delivery.

Program Excellence and Execution

- Own a portfolio of scorecard and supplier performance initiatives, including project plans, roles and responsibilities, timelines, milestones, financial and resource needs, dependencies, risks, and performance metrics.

- Partner with Engineering to manage tool, prioritize requirements, resolve operational issues, strengthen data and process integration.

- Establish and lead the rhythm of business, ensuring stakeholders communicate at the required cadence, decisions are documented, risks are mitigated, and owners are accountable for commitments.

Program Evaluation and Improvement

- Use scorecards, dashboards, scenario analyses, and customer feedback to monitor program health, identify current and future risks, and surface opportunities to streamline, optimize, expand, or retire capabilities.

- Conduct performance-to-value and cost-benefit analyses, including return on investment where appropriate, and contribute clear insights to business reviews and leadership decision-making.

- Identify and deliver automation opportunities, including AI and agentic experiences for supplier surveys, contract analysis, recommendations, and performance insights.

Stakeholder Enablement and Change Leadership

- Define and execute landing, communication, training, and adoption plans tailored to target audiences, business needs, and Microsoft's security principles.

- Evangelize the program and its value through clear storytelling, scorecards, dashboards, presentations, proposals, and other collateral that build stakeholder understanding and commitment.

- Influence senior leaders, engineering partners, operations teams, business owners, and vendors without direct authority, adapting communication and negotiation approaches to reach collaborative solutions.

Capabilities and Skills

- Applies critical judgment, analytical rigor, and structured problem solving to synthesize information, assess risks and alternatives, and translate insights into practical recommendations and sound business decisions.

- Communicates clearly and builds productive relationships across technical, operational, executive, and supplier audiences, using tailored storytelling, negotiation, and influence to align stakeholders and resolve conflict.

- Leads complex cross-functional programs with agility and discipline, connecting business strategy, operational processes, financial value drivers, and systems to drive quality, change adoption, continuous improvement, and measurable outcomes.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications:

- Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 4+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Master's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or a related field and 6+ years of experience in program management, process management, or process improvement; or Bachelor's Degree in one of these fields and 8+ years of relevant experience; or equivalent experience.

- Experience with supplier scorecards, supplier performance management, sourcing, procurement operations, supplier governance, contract lifecycle management, risk, or compliance solutions.

- Experience managing an enterprise technology product or process through strategy, implementation, integration, adoption, run-state, and continuous improvement.

- Experience with Source-to-Pay platforms, procurement technology, workflow automation, process mapping, or related enterprise systems.

- Experience partnering with engineering teams on requirements, prioritization, release planning, service health, security, privacy, and compliance needs.

- Knowledge of artificial intelligence, machine learning, advanced analytics, or agentic solutions and their application to business processes.

- Experience leading complex, cross-functional programs with business, operations, data, engineering, and senior stakeholder groups.

- Experience defining program strategy, success measures, roadmaps, project plans, risks, dependencies, and change or adoption approaches.

- Experience using data, scorecards, dashboards, financial analysis, and performance metrics to identify issues, evaluate value, and influence decisions.

jobs.title: Director, Business Program Management
jobs.description:
Overview
Do you enjoy solving problems, writing software, and working with customers? Do you want to join a team where learning about new technology is part of our work every day? Then, come join us!

The Microsoft Frontier Company team is a global engineering organization that works directly with customers looking to leverage the latest technologies to address their toughest challenges.

We work closely with our customers’ engineers to jointly develop code for cloud-based solutions that can accelerate their organization. We work in collaboration with Microsoft product teams, partners, and open-source communities to empower our customers to do more with the cloud. We develop solutions side-by-side with our customers through collaborative innovation to solve their challenges. This work involves the development of broadly applicable, high-impact solution patterns and open-source software assets that contribute to the Microsoft platform.

As a Director of Business Programs in Frontier Company, you will help build and run the business behind Forward Deployed Engineering, the model we use to put Microsoft engineers inside our customers’ hardest problems. You will shape how work enters the portfolio and what earns priority, set the cadences that keep engineering teams, industry advisors, field teams, partners, and customers working to one playbook and one quality bar, and hold that standard across every team, industry, and region we serve. You will also quantify what the work is worth, translating engineering effort into business outcomes and results that customers and executives can celebrate, and closing the loop so the impact outlasts the engagement.

This is a function being built rather than inherited, and this opportunity will allow you to shape it. You will build deep AI and industry fluency at the center of Microsoft’s most complex customer engagements, sharpen your executive influence as you shape how a global engineering organization measures and preserves the value it creates, and learn how to scale a new operating model from the ground up. You will do it alongside software engineers, technical program managers, data scientists, designers, and customer executives, on a team where new technology, open source, and close collaboration with Microsoft product teams are part of the work every day.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

-----
課題解決やソフトウェア開発が好きで、お客様と直接協働することにやりがいを感じますか？また、新しいテクノロジーを学ぶことが日々の仕事の一部である環境で働きたいと思いますか？そのような方は、ぜひ私たちのチームにご参加ください。Microsoft Frontier Companyチームは、最先端のテクノロジーを活用してお客様の最も困難な課題を解決したいと考える企業と直接協働する、グローバルなエンジニアリング組織です。私たちはお客様のエンジニアと密接に連携し、クラウドベースのソリューションを共同で設計・開発します。Microsoftのプロダクトチーム、パートナー企業、オープンソースコミュニティとも協力しながら、お客様がクラウドの力を最大限活用できるよう支援しています。お客様と並走しながらイノベーションを生み出し、課題解決に取り組むことが私たちの仕事です。この取り組みを通じて、さまざまな業界や顧客に適用可能な高い汎用性とインパクトを持つソリューションパターンや、Microsoftプラットフォームに貢献するオープンソース資産を生み出しています。Frontier CompanyのDirector of Business Programsとして、あなたはForward Deployed Engineering（FDE）の事業運営を構築し、推進する役割を担います。FDEは、Microsoftのエンジニアをお客様の最も難易度の高い課題の解決に直接投入する独自のモデルです。

具体的には、
・どの案件をポートフォリオに取り込む
・かどの案件を優先するか
・エンジニアリングチーム、Industry Advisor、営業チーム、パートナー、お客様が共通の運営モデルと品質基準で動くためのリズム（Cadence）をどのように設計するか
を定義・推進します。

また、技術的な取り組みをビジネス成果へと翻訳し、その価値を定量化することも重要な役割です。お客様や経営層が評価できる成果を可視化し、プロジェクト終了後もその効果が継続する仕組みを構築します。このポジションは、既存の組織や仕組みを引き継ぐのではなく、新たに構築していく役割です。そのため、自ら組織や運営モデルを形作る貴重な機会となります。

この役割を通じて、
・Microsoftの最も複雑な顧客案件の中心でAIおよび業界知識を深める
・グローバルなエンジニアリング組織における価値測定や成果管理の仕組みを設計することで、経営層への影響力を高める
・新しい事業運営モデルをゼロからスケールさせる経験を積む
ことができます。

また、ソフトウェアエンジニア、テクニカルプログラムマネージャー、データサイエンティスト、デザイナー、お客様企業の経営層と日々協働しながら、新技術やオープンソース、Microsoftプロダクトチームとの連携を推進していきます。Microsoftのミッションは、「地球上のすべての人と組織がより多くのことを達成できるよう支援する」ことです。私たちは成長マインドセットを持って学び続け、イノベーションによって他者を支援し、共通の目標達成のために協力します。尊重、誠実さ、説明責任という価値観を基盤に、誰もが活躍できるインクルーシブな文化を築いています。

Responsibilities
- To stay competitive, you will perform program landscape analysis and examine business trends, while contributing to programs impacting Microsoft. You’ll also identify opportunities to develop and improve programs, surfacing upstream insights when delivery outcomes lag, and drive program strategy definition and project plan creation.
- You will drive strategic alignment across engineering teams, industry advisors, field teams, partners, and customers to design crucial programs from initiation to delivery. You’ll also use subject matter expertise to drive the definition and tracking of success criteria and performance metrics at the portfolio level rather than the individual activity level .
- You will set best practices to define and execute on a landing and communication plan, owning the operating cadences and business rhythms that drive clear outcomes during execution. You’ll also use your subject matter expertise to maintain one consistent playbook and quality standard across the portfolio, and to promote the program and gain buy-in from stakeholders, partners, and customers.
- As you oversee a portfolio of projects, you’ll keep programs data-current and progressing against leadership-agreed milestones, communicating status and risk to stakeholders and holding them accountable to following the schedule. You’ll also drive collaboration between teams and maintain the portfolio hygiene that lets the business scale without operational drift.
- You will provide deep expertise to conduct cost-benefit analyses and capture, analyze, and report defensible, quantifiable business results traceable to customer impact, instrumenting return-on-investment frameworks so performance stays observable. You’ll also optimize the use of data analytics to derive insights and identify risks and opportunities, steward the close-out loop so impact is sustained and handed over after delivery, and drive material capability uplift through AI as you influence change management processes in the organization.
- You will embody our culture and values .

ーー

1. プログラム戦略の策定と改善
・市場・業界動向やプログラム全体の状況を分析し、Microsoftに影響を与える重要なプログラムに貢献する
・プログラム改善の機会を特定する
・実行結果が期待に届かない場合、その要因を上流工程まで遡って分析し、改善提案を行う
・プログラム戦略の策定およびプロジェクト計画の作成を推進する

2. ポートフォリオレベルでの戦略的アラインメント
・エンジニアリングチーム、Industry Advisor、営業チーム、パートナー、お客様との戦略的整合性を確立する
・プログラムを企画段階から実行・完了までリードする
・個々の活動ではなく、ポートフォリオ全体の成功指標（Success Criteria）およびKPIの定義と管理を推進する

3. オペレーションモデルと品質基準の確立
・ローンチ計画およびコミュニケーション計画のベストプラクティスを策定する
・明確な成果を生み出すための業務リズム（Business Rhythm）や運営プロセスを設計・管理する
・ポートフォリオ全体で共通のプレイブックと品質基準を維持する
・ステークホルダー、パートナー、お客様からの支持と合意形成を推進する

4. ポートフォリオ運営管理
・プロジェクトポートフォリオ全体を管理する
・データの最新性と品質を維持する
・リーダーシップチームと合意したマイルストーンに対する進捗を管理する
・ステークホルダーへ状況やリスクを適切に報告する
・各チームが計画通りに実行するよう促し、説明責任を徹底する
・事業拡大に伴って運営品質が低下しないよう、継続的な運営改善を行う

5. ビジネス成果の定量化とAI活用推進
・費用対効果分析（Cost-Benefit Analysis）を実施する
・顧客へのインパクトと紐付いた定量的かつ説明可能なビジネス成果を収集・分析・報告する
・ROI（投資対効果）を継続的に測定できるフレームワークを構築する
・データ分析を活用し、リスクや機会を早期に発見する
・プロジェクト終了後も成果が継続するための引き継ぎ・定着化を推進する
・AI活用を通じて組織能力向上を牽引し、変革マネジメントを推進する

6. Microsoftカルチャーの体現
・Microsoftの文化・価値観を体現し、実践する

Qualifications
Required Qualifications (RQs)
- Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Operations, Finance or related field AND 8+ years work experience in program management, process management, process improvement - OR equivalent experience

- Business-level proficiency in both Japanese and English

Additional or Preferred Qualifications (PQs)
- Master's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance or related field AND 8+ years program management experience, process management, process improvement - OR Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance or related field AND 10+ years experience in program management, process management, process improvement

Within Frontier Company, you will find a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives, personal and cultural experiences which are vital to our success with our customers.  It’s an informal and flexible work environment and you’ll be welcome to work in the way that best enables you to get your job done.

jobs.location: United States, Multiple Locations, Multiple Locations
jobs.description:
Overview
The Cloud & AI organization accelerates Microsoft’s mission and bold ambitions to ensure that our company and industry is securing digital technology platforms, devices, and clouds in our customers’ heterogeneous environments, as well as ensuring the security of our own internal estate. Our culture is centered on embracing a growth mindset, a theme of inspiring excellence, and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best each day. In doing so, we create life-changing innovations that impact billions of lives around the world. Microsoft is one of the largest enterprise service companies in the world.

AI-driven vulnerability discovery is producing findings at machine speed against operating structures built for human speed. Cyber Defense Operations (CDO’s) operating model needs to be aligned to this reality. AI is the connecting factor: rapid remediation must absorb machine-speed findings, evictions and escalations must compress response timelines driven by AI-accelerated threats, and CDO’s broader AI adoption needs intentional structure. This role owns that redesign.

We are looking for a Principal Strategic Operations Lead to join the team!

“Strategic Operations” here means designing how CDO operates, not running day-to-day operations. The role identifies where the operating model needs to more closely align with the emerging threat landscape, design the target-state architecture, and build the structures that close the gap. The work begins in the Incident Management portfolio and extends across CDO where cross-functional integration requires broader coordination. This role is expected to grow into a small strategic capability as charters scale.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

Responsibilities
- Identify emerging gaps in CDO’s operating posture, including those created by AI-accelerated threat timelines, and define strategic responses before they become crises.
- Define and drive CDO’s operating model evolution: what needs to change, what needs to be built, and how the organization should sequence the work.
- Advise CISO org leadership on operating model design, organizational integration, and AI adoption strategy based on cross-functional insights and external landscape analysis.
- Design and stand up operating structures for priority strategic projects, then decrease involvement as functional leads take ownership.
- Drive AI adoption strategy for CDO: use-case intake, prioritization frameworks, governance guardrails, and maturity measurement.
- Serve as the connective layer across functional leads, ensuring dependencies are visible and cross-cutting work streams stay synchronized.
- Surface early signals when a charter is stalling — missed deadlines, shifting goalposts, adoption gaps — and escalate with clarity and recommended action.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
- Bachelor's Degree AND 6+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development - OR equivalent experience.

- 3+ years of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.

- Proven ability to run a portfolio of stakeholder relationships and drive structured collaboration frameworks that reduce friction.
- Excellent executive communication: ability to synthesize ambiguity into crisp narratives and decision points.
- Operational rigor and systems thinking (service rhythms, governance patterns, repeatable processes).
