Overview
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day. Microsoft Cloud Operations and Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than one hundred datacenters and one million servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts, who work tirelessly to support digital services for more than one billion customers and twenty million businesses in over ninety countries worldwide.
Within CO+I, the Core Datacenter Services (CDS) team is responsible for improving the availability, resilience, and efficiency of Microsoft’s global cloud infrastructure. We are seeking a Senior Director, MRO Supply Chain - Datacenter Operations to lead the end-to-end supply chain for maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) spare parts supporting datacenters globally. Additionally, this role has responsibility for destruction equipment strategy and qualification that includes the spare part planning and fulfilment of maintenance standards within our datacenters and circular centers. This senior leader will set the vision, operating model, and transformation agenda for the function, building the capabilities, systems, partnerships, and talent required to plan, source, position, move, replenish, repair, recover, and manage critical spare parts throughout their lifecycle. The role is accountable for supply and demand planning, logistics, warehousing, supply network design, inventory strategy, supplier execution, and service performance in support of reliable datacenter operations and Microsoft’s AI and cloud growth.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities
- Set and communicate the global end-to-end MRO spare-parts supply chain vision, strategy, standards, and multi-year transformation roadmap, aligned to CO+I priorities, datacenter reliability, AI capacity growth, company goals, financial objectives, and customer commitments.
- Lead, develop, and inspire a geographically distributed organization of supply chain professionals and leaders. Establish clear accountability, strengthen succession and talent pipelines, coach and mentor team members and leaders, and create an inclusive, high-performance culture with efficient processes through significant change.
- Own end-to-end supply chain performance for MRO spare parts across demand and supply planning, sourcing and supplier execution, inventory management, warehousing, transportation and logistics, supply network design, deployment, returns, repair loops, recovery, and end-of-life disposition.
- Develop and execute supply-planning targets and replenishment standards across all nodes in the supply chain. Deliver measurable improvement in availability, On Time in Full (OTIF), inventory turns, excess and obsolescence, expedite cost, and total cost to serve.

- Design and optimize the global supply network, including stocking locations, replenishment flows, service levels, lead-time strategies, transportation models, and resilience measures. Balance availability, risk, cost, sustainability, and working capital.
- Lead day-to-day and strategic relationships with third parties, suppliers, and logistics partners to ensure safety, security, quality, resilience, compliance, capacity, and service performance while maximizing execution and driving continuous improvement.
- Escalate and resolve field supply chain issues; prioritize service based on material lead times, criticality, and availability; analyze material consumption trends; review engineering change orders affecting spare parts; and ensure hardware compatibility and lifecycle readiness.
- Define risk-based strategies for critical spares, long-lead components, lifecycle transitions, repair and return loops, substitutions, constrained supply, and excess and obsolete inventory.
- Implement measurement frameworks and performance-management mechanisms that enable data-driven decision-making, evaluate business and supplier performance, identify optimization opportunities, and provide clear ownership and disciplined execution.
- Serve as the executive expert in the tools and processes used to manage supply. Lead the transformation of processes, data, governance, and digital capabilities through automation, integrated systems, advanced analytics, scenario planning, and scalable inventory solutions.

- Ensure supply chain operations meet Microsoft safety, security, regulatory, and business-continuity requirements, with safe and secure solutions for internal and external customer commitments as the highest priority.

jobs.title: Principal Transformation Partner
jobs.location: Belgium, Brussels Region, Brussels; Norway, Oslo, Oslo; Denmark, Capital Region, Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Overview
Microsoft Frontier Company is redefining how enterprises transform — bringing agentic AI, cloud-scale computing, data, simulation, and human expertise together so customers turn ambition into measurable business impact. As customers look to reinvent how work gets done — redesigning business processes, operating models, and human-agent ways of working across industries and functions, from financial services and telecommunications to manufacturing, retail, the public sector, and R&D-intensive discovery — they need more than a platform. They need partners fluent in both business and technology who can turn strategic ambition into working, governed, and economically sound solutions. This role has three dimensions: shaping customer outcomes, orchestrating and guiding delivery and building the repeatable motions that scale transformation.

We are seeking a Principal Transformation Partner with the mindset, executive presence, and leadership to define and shape ambiguous, first-of-kind transformation opportunities. You will work directly with business and technology leaders, account teams, industry specialists, and Microsoft product engineering to set the direction for high-value scenarios and turn a customer’s strategic ambition into executable transformation blueprints. Operating as part of — and often orchestrating — a multidisciplinary Transformation Squad, you serve as the bridge between business outcomes, AI-native operating models, and Microsoft’s technologies, shaping strategy from pre-sales through delivery and converting them into repeatable motions that scale across customers and industries.

This is a role for builders who thrive in ambiguity, move comfortably from high-level customer needs to whiteboard to working solution, and are energized by solving complex problems in the real world. You will help customers reimagine how people and AI agents work together — redesigning processes and experiences so the new operating model is intuitive, governed, and economically sound — while defining the repeatable patterns, product feedback, and delivery motions that others adopt to scale this frontier AI business. Every solution begins with AI and human collaboration, with explicit return on investment designed in from the start. If you are excited to co-create with customers, unlock new possibilities, and help establish one of Microsoft’s most strategic AI growth motions, this role is for you.

This is a business-and-technology leadership role, not a deep technical SME position. You are conversant across both worlds — setting direction in architecture and technology discussions and translating between business outcomes and technical delivery . You guide and orchestrate delivery rather than run it yourself. Your edge is connecting ambition, value, and technology at scale, and mobilizing the right specialists across the engagement.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities
Transformation Leadership & Squad Orchestration

- Owns the customer engagement and vision as the trusted advisor across the full lifecycle — shaping ambiguous, first-of-kind opportunities, translating executive ambition into outcomes, and holding continuity of vision from pre-sales through delivery.

- Sets the direction for ambiguous, first-of-kind transformation: turning strategic ambition into an executable blueprint that defines the business processes, operating model, and human-agent workflows to be redesigned and the measurable outcomes each change will deliver.

- Partners across teams to define AI-native human-agent operating models and shape seamless experiences that accelerate adoption and drive new ways of working..

- Orchestrates the One Microsoft team — determining squad composition and sequencing the capabilities across pre-sales and delivery, and often leading the trio within Frontier Co..

- Sets the repeatable engagement method for ambiguous, first-of-kind opportunities — shaping the transformation vision, directing the AI maturity assessment, driving bold ideas, and using rapid prototyping to build conviction  towards a new AI-enabled operating models.

Understanding Customer/Partner Technical Environment

- Gathers and synthesizes customer and partner insights from a broad range of stakeholders, including the business sponsor, to shape both the definition and ongoing execution of the engagement. Adapts business models, plans, and solutions in response to those insights.

- Uses evidence-based approach to function as a customer advocate and drives awareness of insights with a view for improving Microsoft technologies, products, services, and offerings such that they can better meet customer/partner needs.

Shaping the Architecture for Business Outcomes

- Sets the architecture direction from the business outcome inward, working with — and often steering — the delivery and platform architects  who own the technical design and build. Holds a single gate over every architectural choice — the value of the unit of work — so each component earns its place by the outcome it delivers, not by technical elegance.

- Owns the value hypothesis and validates the baseline and target KPIs for the transformation, and holds the causal link between the unit of work and those outcomes — so every agentic task, workflow, and component traces to a measurable business result. Owns this value and outcome traceability across the engagement; the technical requirements and design artifacts are owned by the platform and delivery architects.

- Directs and sequences proofs of concept (POCs) and MVPs delivered by the technical specialists, using each to prove the causal link between the unit of work and the target KPIs — and to validate the unit economics, including token economics, so the solution is viable at scale.

- Works with the business sponsor and stakeholders to ratify the outcomes, constraints, and success measures, and ensures acceptance criteria trace to the value hypothesis rather than to technical output alone. The technical requirements/constraints traceability and test execution are run by the delivery and platform architects.

- Owns a realistically costed solution approach anchored to the value case and its economics, balancing existing offerings with new, first-of-kind approaches where the scenario demands. Orchestrates the build across Enterprise AI Platforms, FDE, and Regional Delivery through to live operations — steering and sequencing rather than running the build — and keeps the delivered unit of work aligned to the committed outcome.

- Anticipates and removes the scenarios that could slow or impede pre-sales and delivery, engaging the broader Microsoft team on technical blockers and the account/project team on non-technical issues. Aligns specialists and coordinates disparate approaches into a single plan of action, escalating only genuinely cross-organizational risks.

- Works in close collaboration with the Project Manager and Account Team to categorize and communicate business and technical risks. Identifies risks, defines the risk mitigation activities that are foundational to the project plan, and defines the risk contingency plans to be invoked should a risk occur.

Practice Development

- Originates new intellectual property and reusable assets that are adopted beyond the original engagement, drives product and engineering feedback from customer evidence, and champions Recommended Practices across pre-sales and delivery. Leads internal and external communities.

Trusted Advisor

- Builds and leverages a network of internal and external relationships to influence executive and principal-level stakeholders, unblock strategic issues, and align multiple organizations. Develops deep knowledge of Microsoft’s technologies, products, and services in order to communicate Microsoft’s mission, strategy, and capabilities.

- Uses evidence-based arguments that articulate complex concepts in a simple manner to respectfully challenge Microsoft and customers/partners when a decision or course of action will not produce optimal results. Escalates scenarios as appropriate. Serves as the "technical conscience" to challenge the status quo and unrealistic expectations. Resolves conflicts and seeks resolution to balance the overall outcome when needed.

- Understands competitor solutions and identifies how customer business value can be driven through Microsoft's offerings. Demonstrates the benefits of the solution in customer/partner conversations.

Thought Leadership

- Shares ideas, insight, and technical input with virtual team members (e.g., Account team, enterprise channel managers) using a working knowledge of specific Microsoft architectures and other relevant products.

- Participates in external architect community events (e.g., conferences, seminars, technical meetups, Webcasts, blogs, hackathons) and shares learnings with internal team.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, or related field AND extensive experience spanning business and technology transformation — consulting, solution shaping, digital and AI transformation, and/or a relevant technology domain — with the ability to set direction credibly across both business and technical topics.
- OR equivalent experience.

Come build community, explore your passions and do your best work at Microsoft. This opportunity will allow you to bring your aspirations, talent, potential - and excitement for the journey ahead.

They’ll get to submit preferences for teams that interest them most across corporate finance, sales and product groups like Azure, M365, and XBOX, all while using best-in-class AI tools to solve complex business problems. As an FRP Analyst, you can expect to develop your finance skills rapidly, contribute meaningfully, and interact with senior leaders, gaining insights and mentorship to help you accelerate your career.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees, we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. jobs.title: Head of Internal Audit, MIPSL and Audit Program Management
jobs.location: Ireland, Multiple Locations, Multiple Locations; Ireland, Dublin, Dublin
jobs.description:
Overview
Do you enjoy working with dynamic people to solve complex business problems? If you love a challenge, have a passion for creating clarity, program management, and cross-group collaboration, we want you. This role will serve as the Head of Internal Audit for Microsoft Ireland Payment Services Limited (MIPSL). MIPSL’s Internal Audit function reports into and is supported by the Microsoft Internal Audit Group. The Head of MIPSL Internal Audit will be approved by the MIPSL Board and the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) in line with the CBI’s Pre-Approved Control Function (PCF) requirements. In addition, this role will lead selective, outcome-focused audit programs across other business functions within Microsoft, developing and managing risk-based coverage in partnership with senior leadership.

Responsibilities
MIPSL Head of Internal Audit (CBI PCF-13)
- Establish and maintain the MIPSL internal audit function; set and communicate the objectives, vision and strategy of internal audit; prepare and submit an internal audit charter for MIPSL Board approval setting out audit standards and governance arrangements.

- Develop and implement the MIPSL Internal Audit Plan, communicate and agree audit scope and terms of reference with department managers prior to commencement of audit work; leverage Microsoft Internal Audit resources to deliver the plan.
- Provide quarterly and annual reports to the MIPSL Board on regular and special internal audit assignments, if any.
- Maintain independence, in particular to ensure ability to appropriately deliver role as Head of Internal Audit for MIPSL
- Make constructive proposals to the MIPSL Board for minimization of risk, remediation of deficiencies and improvement of systems, processes and controls.
- Participate in the MIPSL Audit Committee, keeping the Committee fully up to date on all internal audit matters.
- Keep up to date with emerging external (markets, regulations) and internal (business, technology, operational risk events) factors, standards and practices to identify meaningful themes and trends in the payments industry; regularly review and update the internal audit framework and audit plan so it remains current and fit-for-purpose for the nature, scale and risk profile of MIPSL’s business.
- Actively engage in financial services Internal Audit industry groups, ensuring MIPSL’s Internal Audit function is up to speed on regulatory and legislative matters impacting the payments sector in the EEA.
- Conduct special audits, investigations and advisory assignments as agreed with the MIPSL Board, the MIPSL Audit Committee or as directed by the regulator.
- Build and maintain a high-performing financial services Internal Audit capability through the leadership and training of appropriately skilled resources, ensuring the function possesses the expertise and professional competencies to deliver the Internal Audit Plan.

Selective Microsoft Business Functions Audit Programs (Non-MIPSL)
- Analyze risk trends to the business to build the annual plan for assigned business function programs, identifying trends and potential blind spots for senior leadership and the Microsoft Board of Directors.
- Lead annual program and project planning by partnering with the business to ensure key risks are addressed by the audit project.
- Provide oversight on project execution, ensuring it focuses on key risks to Microsoft.
- Influence management as a trusted advisor to clarify risks to their business and where there may be potential blind spots.
- Ensure clear and concise audit reporting of risks tested during the audit; analyze and advise management on whether their planned actions will mitigate identified risks.
- Report clear and concise analysis of audit results to identify trends and blind spots for senior leadership and the Microsoft Board of Directors.

Leadership and Culture
- Build business acumen, foster an inclusive culture, and instill a risk mindset across the audit team.
- Embody Microsoft values and “One Microsoft,” while embracing a growth mindset and driving impact. Champion an inclusive and collaborative workplace where everyone can be their best.
- Raise the technical knowledge of self and group on assigned risk areas through training and continuous professional development.

Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications :
- Hold a relevant professional qualification (e.g. CIA, ACA, ACCA, CPA, CIMA, CISA or equivalent) and have relevant experience in Internal Audit, Risk, or Assurance, including experience in a senior audit leadership role within regulated financial services.
- Deep understanding of the Irish and European regulatory landscape for payment institutions and financial services.
- Proven experience leading Internal Audit functions within regulated financial services, including developing and executing risk-based audit plans, maintaining professional standards and driving continuous improvement.
- Expertise in evaluating governance, risk management and internal control frameworks, identifying control weaknesses, conducting root cause analysis and providing pragmatic, risk-focused recommendations in line with industry best practice and regulatory expectations.

The following are preferred:
- Previous experience holding a PCF role approved by the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) with responsibility for Internal Audit within a regulated financial services firm.
- Strong professional judgement, integrity and independence, with the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders and escalate material issues appropriately to executive and board-level forums.
- Proven program management skills, with a record of effectively managing an audit or compliance program in a decentralized, empowered and constantly changing environment.
- Excellent communication and presentation skills, including persuasive delivery of controversial messages to senior management and experience reporting to Boards, Audit Committees, executive leadership and regulators on audit opinions, findings and emerging risks.
- Ability to assess business models, emerging risks and strategic initiatives, ensuring audit coverage remains aligned to organizational objectives and regulatory expectations.
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience in drafting advisory memorandums of findings, conclusions, and recommendations for management action plans.
- Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 20% of the year.
- A BS/BA degree in related field
- Advanced degree
